p.src: The tale tells how the Bull Demon King caught up with the Great Sage Sun and saw him walking cheerfully along with the Plantain Fan over his shoulder. The Demon King was greatly alarmed and thought, “So the macaque has even wheedled the method of using it out of her. If I ask him for it to his face, he certainly will not give it to me; and if he fans me once and sends me a hundred and eight thousand li away, would that not be playing straight into his hands? I have heard that the Tang Monk is waiting on the main road. His second disciple, the pig spirit, and his third, the river-sand spirit, both met me back when I was still living as a demon. I shall take the pig spirit’s shape and trick him in return. The macaque will surely be so delighted by his success that he will not guard against me closely.” A fine Demon King he was! He too knew the seventy-two transformations, and his martial skill equaled the Great Sage’s, though his body was somewhat large and ungainly. He was not quite so quick, nimble, or agile; he concealed his precious sword, recited a spell, shook himself, and changed at once into Bajie’s very likeness. Taking a shortcut, he came straight toward the Great Sage and called, “Elder Brother, here I am!”

p.src: The Great Sage was indeed delighted. As the ancients said, “A victorious cat is as jubilant as a tiger.” Relying solely on his prowess, he gave no thought to the newcomer’s intentions. Seeing Bajie’s likeness, he called, “Brother, where are you going?” The Bull Demon King improvised smoothly: “Master saw that you had not returned for so long. Fearing that the Bull Demon King was too formidable for you to defeat and that you might not obtain his treasure, he sent me to meet you.” The Pilgrim laughed. “No need to worry. I have already succeeded.” The Bull King asked, “How did you get it?” The Pilgrim replied, “That old bull fought me for a hundred rounds or so, with neither of us gaining the advantage. Then he broke away from me and went to the bottom of the Emerald Wave Pool at Tumbledown Mountain to drink with a band of flood-dragon and dragon spirits. I followed him secretly, changed into a crab, stole the Golden-Eyed Beast that Parts the Waters which he rode, assumed the old bull’s appearance, and went straight to Plantain Cave to deceive the Rakshasa Woman. The woman and old Sun played at being husband and wife for a while, and by this stratagem I tricked the fan from her.” The Bull King said, “You have certainly taken great pains. You have labored far too hard, Elder Brother. Let me carry the fan.” The Great Sage Sun could not tell true from false and never imagined such a trick, so he handed him the fan.

Taking it in hand, he made some unknown finger sign, and it became once more as small as an apricot leaf; then he resumed his true form. He opened his mouth and cursed, “You insolent macaque! Do you recognize me?” When the Pilgrim saw him, he regretted his mistake and thought, “This was my own fault.” With a bitter groan, he stamped his foot and cried aloud, “Ah! All these years I have hunted wild geese, and today a gosling has pecked out my eye!” His fury exploded like thunder. Drawing his iron staff, he struck straight at the Demon King’s head; but the Demon King gave him a stroke with the fan. Little did he know that when the Great Sage had earlier changed into a tiny insect and entered the Rakshasa Woman’s belly, he had held the Wind-Fixing Pearl in his mouth and accidentally swallowed it. p.src: Let us leave the two of them locked in inconclusive combat. The tale turns to the Tang Monk, sitting beside the road, oppressed first by the scorching heat and then by anxious thirst. He asked the local god of the Mountain of Flames, “May I ask, honored deity, how great are the Bull Demon King’s powers?” The local god replied, “The Bull King’s supernatural abilities are formidable and his magic boundless. He is truly a match for the Great Sage Sun.” Tripitaka said, “Wukong travels swiftly. Ordinarily he can cover two thousand li and return in an instant. Why has he now been gone an entire day? He must surely be locked in combat with the Bull King.” He called, “Wuneng, Wujing—which of you will go to meet your elder brother? Should you encounter the enemy, exert yourself to help him. Obtain the fan, relieve me of this torment, and let us cross the mountain and resume our journey as soon as possible.” Bajie said, “It is late today. I have been thinking that I should go meet him, but I do not know the road to Mount Thunderclap.” The local god said, “This humble god knows the way. Let the Curtain-Lifting General remain with your master, while I go with you.” Tripitaka was delighted. “I am much obliged to you, honored deity. When the deed is done, I shall thank you again.”

p.src: Bajie roused his spirits, tightened his black brocade robe, shouldered his rake, and rose into the clouds with the local god, heading straight back east. As they traveled, they suddenly heard loud battle cries amid rolling gales. Bajie halted his cloud to look and saw that it was the Pilgrim Sun fighting the Bull King. The local god said, “Marshal of the Heavenly Reeds, why do you not go forward? What are you waiting for?” The fool drew his nine-pronged rake and shouted fiercely, “Elder Brother, here I am!” The Pilgrim said bitterly, “You clod! What great trouble you have caused me!” Bajie replied, “Master sent me to meet you. Since I did not know the mountain road, we discussed it for a long while before asking the local god to guide me, and that is why I came late. How have I caused great trouble?” The Pilgrim said, “I do not blame you for arriving late. It is this insolent bull who has behaved outrageously. I had contrived to get the fan from the Rakshasa Woman, but this rogue changed into your likeness and claimed he had come to meet me. In my momentary delight I handed the fan straight into his hands. Then he revealed his true form and began contending with old Sun here. That is how the great matter was ruined.” Hearing this, Bajie flew into a rage. Raising his rake, he cursed the Bull King to his face: “You plague-stricken, bloated brute! How dare you assume your ancestor’s appearance, deceive my elder brother, and sow discord between us?” Just watch him rain down wild blows with his rake, caring neither for head nor face.

p.src: The Bull King, for one thing, was weary in strength and exhausted in spirit after fighting the Pilgrim for an entire day; for another, Bajie’s rake was so ferocious that he could not parry it. Defeated, he turned and fled. But the local god of the Mountain of Flames appeared with his spirit soldiers and barred his way, saying, “Great King of Mighty Strength, stay your hand. Tang Tripitaka is going to the Western Heaven to fetch the scriptures. There is no god who does not protect him and no celestial power that does not aid him. All Three Realms know of it, and all ten directions support him. Quickly bring out the Plantain Fan and extinguish the flames, so that he may cross the mountain early, free from calamity and obstruction; otherwise Heaven will call you to account for your crimes, and you will surely be put to death.” The Bull King replied, “You local god understand nothing of justice. That damned monkey seized my son, insulted my concubine, and deceived my wife. Again and again he has acted without principle. I would gladly swallow him whole, turn him into dung, and feed it to the dogs. How could I possibly lend him my treasure?”

p.src: The Demon King fought fiercely for supremacy, battling as he went; they fought through the night without either gaining the upper hand, until day broke once more. Ahead lay the entrance to his Cloud-Touching Cave on Mount Thunderclap. The three combatants, together with the local god and the ghostly soldiers, raised such a deafening uproar that Princess Jade Countenance was startled and ordered a maid to see who was making all the noise. Presently a gatekeeping imp came to report, “Our lord is fighting that thunder-god-faced fellow from yesterday, a long-snouted, big-eared monk, and the local god of the Mountain of Flames with his company.” On hearing this, Princess Jade Countenance immediately ordered all the greater and lesser chiefs guarding the outer grounds to take up spears and swords and go to his aid. They mustered a motley band of over a hundred. Each strutted forth in high spirits, flourishing spear or staff, and together they announced, “Great King and lord, we have come especially to assist you by our lady’s command from within!” The Bull King was delighted. “Excellent! Excellent!” he cried. The whole horde of demons surged forward, hacking wildly. Caught unprepared, Bajie dragged his rake behind him and fled in defeat. The Great Sage mounted his somersault cloud and leapt free of the encirclement. The ghostly soldiers likewise scattered in every direction. Victorious, the old bull gathered his demon host and returned to the cave, whose gates he shut fast. Of this no more need be said.

p.src: Pilgrim said, “That brute is truly valiant. Old Sun began fighting him around the Hour of the Monkey yesterday, and even by nightfall the outcome was still undecided. Fortunately, you two came to relieve me. Yet after fighting so bitterly for half a day and a whole night, he still showed no sign of fatigue. And that band of lesser demons just now was fierce and sturdy too. Now he has barred the cave gate and refuses to come out. What are we to do?” Bajie said, “Brother, you left Master at the Hour of the Snake yesterday. How was it that you did not begin fighting him until the Hour of the Monkey? Where were you during those two or three double-hours?” Pilgrim replied, “After parting from you, I reached this mountain in no time and met a woman. When I questioned her, she turned out to be his beloved concubine, Princess Jade Countenance. I frightened her with my iron staff, and she ran into the cave and called the Bull King out. He and I traded barbed words and shouted at each other for a while. Then we came to blows and fought for about one double-hour. In the midst of the fighting, someone came to invite him to a banquet. I followed him to the bottom of the Emerald-Wave Pool on Craggy Mountain, changed into a crab to gather information, stole his Golden-Eyed Beast that Parts the Waters, assumed the Bull King’s appearance, and returned to Plantain Cave on Mount Emerald Cloud. There I deceived the Rakshasi and tricked the fan out of her. Once outside, I tried out its method, made the fan grow large, but did not know how to shrink it again. Just as I was carrying it away, he disguised himself with your face and tricked it back from me. That is why I was delayed for two or three double-hours.”

p.src: The two of them led the local god and the ghostly soldiers forward together. Wielding rake and swinging iron staff, they smashed the front gate of Cloud-Touching Cave to splinters with a deafening clatter. The chiefs guarding the outer grounds trembled with fear and rushed inside to report, “Great King! Sun Wukong has led his host here and smashed through the front gate!” At that moment the Bull King was recounting the affair in detail to Princess Jade Countenance and bitterly resenting Sun the Pilgrim. On hearing that the front gate had been smashed, he flew into a rage, hastily donned his armor, seized his iron cudgel, and came storming out from within, cursing, “You vile macaque! Who do you think you are, to come raging to my very door and smash my gate?” Bajie stepped forward and hurled abuse: “You damned old hidebound brute! p.src: Pilgrim saw him and laughed. “Bajie, the old bull has escaped.” The idiot had no notion what he meant, nor could the local god understand. They all peered east and west, searching wildly around Mount Thunderclap. Pilgrim pointed and said, “Is that not he flying through the sky?” Bajie said, “That is a swan.” Pilgrim replied, “It is precisely the old bull in disguise.” The local god asked, “If that is so, what should we do?” Pilgrim said, “You two fight your way through this gate, wipe out the demon horde without mercy, tear down his lair, and cut off his road of return. Old Sun will go and match transformations with him.” Bajie and the local god obeyed and stormed through the cave gate. Of them no more need be said.

p.src: The Great Sage put away his gold-banded staff, formed a hand seal, recited a spell, shook himself, and changed into an eastern sea falcon. With a whoosh of his wings he pierced the heart of the clouds, swooped down backward, landed upon the swan, clutched its neck, and pecked at its eyes. The Bull King knew that this too was a transformation of Sun the Pilgrim. He hurriedly shook his wings, changed into a yellow eagle, wheeled around, and pecked at the eastern sea falcon. Pilgrim then changed into a black phoenix that relentlessly pursued the yellow eagle. The Bull King recognized it and changed again, this time into a white crane. With one long cry, he flew southward. Pilgrim steadied himself, shook out his plumage, and changed into a vermilion phoenix, which gave a ringing cry. When the white crane saw the phoenix, king of all birds before whom no feathered creature dared stir rashly, it swept its wings and plunged down the cliff. Changing its form, it became a musk deer and nibbled grass before the precipice with sidelong, furtive glances. Pilgrim recognized him, folded his wings, and descended. He changed into a hungry tiger, lashing its tail and pounding its paws as it rushed to devour the deer. The Demon King lost his composure and changed into a great golden, spotted leopard to maul the hungry tiger. Seeing this, Pilgrim turned into the wind, tossed his head, and changed into a golden-eyed suanni. Its voice was like a thunderclap, its brow iron and its head bronze, and it wheeled around to devour the great leopard. Hard pressed, the Bull King changed again into a man-bear, which charged at full stride to seize the suanni. Pilgrim rolled over and changed into a mangy elephant, with a trunk like a long snake and tusks like bamboo shoots. Unfurling its trunk, it tried to coil it around the man-bear.

From head to tail he was over a thousand zhang long, and from hoof to back eight hundred zhang high. He shouted at the Pilgrim, “You insolent ape! p.src: The two displayed their mighty powers and fought for supremacy halfway up the mountain, alarming all the passing deities of the void, together with the Gold-Headed Guardian, the Six Jia and Six Ding, and the eighteen guardian arhats, who all came to surround the demon king. The demon king showed no fear at all. See how he thrust east and west, driving his two straight, gleaming iron horns back and forth; he butted south and charged north, while his stiff tail, bristling with hair and bulging with sinews, lashed from side to side. Great Sage Sun met him head-on while the host of gods attacked from every side. Hard pressed, the Bull King rolled on the ground, resumed his ordinary form, and fled toward Plantain-Fan Cave. The Pilgrim also dismissed his colossal manifestation and pursued him with the assembled gods. The demon king burst into the cave, shut the gate, and refused to come out. The whole company encircled Emerald Cloud Mountain so tightly that not even water could have leaked through.

p.src: Just as they were all attacking the gate, they suddenly heard Bajie arriving noisily with the local god and his spirit soldiers. Seeing him, the Pilgrim asked, “How did matters go at Cloud-Touching Cave?” Bajie laughed. “I killed the old bull’s wife with one blow of my rake. When I stripped open her clothes and looked, she proved to be a jade-faced vixen spirit. That horde of lesser demons—all manner of donkeys, mules, calves, bulls, badgers, foxes, raccoon dogs, roe deer, sheep, tigers, elks, and deer—has been completely exterminated. We also set fire to the chambers and galleries of their cave dwelling. The local god said the bull had another household living on this mountain, so we came here to sweep it away as well.” The Pilgrim said, “Worthy brother, you have rendered fine service. Excellent, excellent! I merely matched transformations with that old bull and have yet to defeat him. He transformed into a white bull of immeasurable size, and I assumed a body that modeled heaven and conformed to earth. While we were locked in combat, the gods graciously descended and surrounded him for a long while; but he resumed his original form and fled into the cave.” Bajie asked, “Is that Plantain-Fan Cave?” The Pilgrim replied, “It is indeed, it is indeed. The Rakshasi woman is in there.” Bajie said fiercely, “If that is so, why not smash our way in, exterminate the wretch, and demand the fan? Why let him linger there, grow wiser, and exchange tender words with his wife?”

p.src: Good old Idiot roused his martial fury, raised his rake, and struck the gate. With a tremendous crash, he brought down one side of the stone cliff together with the gate. The serving girl hurriedly reported in alarm, “Master, I do not know who has smashed the entire front gate.” The Bull King had only just run inside and, still panting, was telling the Rakshasi woman about his struggle with Pilgrim Sun over the fan. On hearing the report, he flew into a rage, spat the fan out of his mouth, and handed it to the Rakshasi woman. Taking the fan in her hand, the Rakshasi woman said with tears filling her eyes, “My lord, give this fan to that ape and have him withdraw his forces.” The Bull King said, “My lady, the object may be small, but the hatred runs deep. Sit here awhile and wait for me to go contend with him once more.” The demon readjusted his armor, selected a pair of precious swords, and strode out through the gate. He came upon Bajie battering the gate with his rake. Without a word, the old bull drew his swords and chopped straight at his head. Bajie raised his rake to meet the blow and retreated several steps out through the gate, where the Great Sage was already swinging his cudgel down at the Bull King’s head. The Bull Demon mounted a violent wind, leaped clear of the cave dwelling, and once more confronted them atop Emerald Cloud Mountain. p.src: The Bull King fought with reckless disregard for his life. After more than fifty rounds he could resist no longer, lost the battle, and fled north. But the Mighty Vajra of Unbridled Dharma and Vast Supernatural Power from Demon-Secret Cliff on Mount Wutai was already blocking his way. He shouted, “Bull Demon, where are you going? Buddha Shakyamuni sent me to spread a net across heaven and earth and capture you here.” As he spoke, the Great Sage, Bajie, and the assembled gods came racing up behind. The demon king wheeled around in panic and fled south, only to run into the Vajra of Infinite Dharma Power and Supreme Attainment from Cool Cave on Mount Emei, who barred his way and shouted, “By command of the Buddha, I am waiting here expressly to seize you.” The Bull King’s heart quailed and his legs weakened. He hastily turned and fled east, but there he met the Great-Power Vajra, Vaiśravaṇa, from Ear-Rubbing Cliff on Mount Sumeru, who blocked him and shouted, “Where are you going, old bull? The Tathagata secretly commanded me to come and capture you.” The Bull King recoiled in terror and fled west, only to meet the Ever-Abiding Vajra, Indestructible Honored King, from Golden-Cloud Ridge on Mount Kunlun, who opposed him and shouted, “Where else does this wretch think he can escape? I received the Buddha’s personal word at the Great Thunderclap Monastery in the Western Heaven and stand guard here. Who would let you pass?”

While he was in a panic, he again heard the Pilgrim leading the host in pursuit, so he mounted a cloud and fled upward. But Pagoda-Bearing Heavenly King Li and Prince Nezha were there with the Fish-Belly Yaksha and the Mighty-Spirit Divine General, screening off the sky. They called, “Hold there! Hold there! By decree of the Jade Emperor, we have come expressly to exterminate you.” Driven to desperation, the Bull King shook himself as before and transformed once more into a great white bull, thrusting his two iron horns at the Heavenly King. The Heavenly King struck at him with his saber. Pilgrim Sun arrived close behind. Prince Nezha called loudly, “Great Sage, forgive me for not saluting while clad in armor. Yesterday my unworthy father and I saw the Buddha Tathagata issue a dispatch reporting to the Jade Emperor that the Tang monk was blocked at the Mountain of Flames and that Great Sage Sun was finding it difficult to subdue the Bull Demon King. The Jade Emperor then issued a decree specially ordering my father to lead his forces here to assist you.” The Pilgrim said, “This wretch’s powers are considerable, and now he has transformed into such a body. What are we to do with him?” The prince smiled. “Have no doubts, Great Sage. Watch me capture him.”

p.src: The Prince immediately cried, “Transform!” He transformed into a being with three heads and six arms, sprang through the air onto the Bull King’s back, and swept his Demon-Slaying Sword across the neck, severing the bull’s head before anyone knew it. The Heavenly King sheathed his blade, and only then exchanged greetings with Pilgrim. Yet another head pushed out from the Bull King’s neck stump, breathing black vapor from its mouth and shooting golden light from its eyes. Nezha struck it off with another stroke, but where the head fell, yet another emerged. He struck more than ten times in succession, and more than ten heads grew back at once. Nezha took out his fire wheels and hung them upon the old bull’s horns, then blew forth true fire. The roaring flames scorched the Bull King until he thrashed and bellowed wildly, tossing his head and lashing his tail. Just as he tried to transform and escape, Pagoda-Bearing Heavenly King Li fixed the Demon-Revealing Mirror upon his true form. Unable to move or find any means of escape, he could only cry, “Spare my life! I am willing to submit to the Buddhist faith.” Nezha said, “If you value your life, bring out the fan at once.” The Bull King said, “The fan is kept by my wife in our mountain home.”

She bound up her black hair like a Daoist nun and dressed in plain white like a Buddhist mendicant, then came out carrying in both hands the plantain fan, some twelve feet long. I willingly offer this fan so that Uncle Sun may accomplish his task.” Pilgrim stepped forward and received the fan, then mounted auspicious clouds with the whole company and headed straight back east.

p.src: Now Tripitaka and Sha Monk stood for a while and sat for a while as they awaited Pilgrim. When he failed to return for so long, how anxious they became! Suddenly they saw auspicious clouds filling the sky and blessed radiance covering the earth, drifting nearer as the host of gods approached. Alarmed, the elder said, “Wujing, what divine army is coming over there?” Recognizing them, Sha Monk said, “Master, those are the Four Great Vajra Guardians, the Gold-Headed Guardian, the Six Jia and Six Ding, the temple-protecting guardian deities, and all the gods who patrol these parts. The one leading the bull is Third Prince Nezha; the one holding the mirror is Pagoda-Bearing Heavenly King Li. Eldest Brother carries the plantain fan, while Second Brother and the local god follow behind. All the rest are divine guardian troops.” On hearing this, Tripitaka changed into his Vairocana cap and put on his kasaya. Together with Wujing he bowed in welcome to the holy beings and offered thanks, saying, “What virtue or ability does this disciple possess that I should dare trouble all you honored saints to descend to the mortal world?” The Four Great Vajra Guardians said, “Rejoice, holy monk, for your great undertaking is nearly complete. We were sent by the Buddha’s decree to assist you. You must devote your full strength to your cultivation and never grow indolent for even an instant.” Tripitaka clicked his teeth in reverence, bowed his head to the ground, and pledged his whole person and life to the command.

p.src: Pilgrim said, “Rakshasi, why are you still standing here instead of going on your way?” The Rakshasi knelt and said, “I beg the Great Sage to show mercy and return my fan to me.” Bajie shouted, “You shameless wretch! You do not know your place. It is enough that we have spared your life, yet you still ask for the fan? Once we have crossed the mountain, can we not sell it and buy ourselves some refreshments? After all the energy and strength we have spent, why should we give it back to you? It is drizzling now—why have you not gone home?” The Rakshasi bowed again and said, “Great Sage, you originally said that you would return it after fanning out the fire. After all that has happened today, it is truly too late for regret. It was only because I behaved without openness or honor that so many forces had to be mobilized and put to such trouble. We too have cultivated ourselves into human form; it is only that we have not yet attained the true fruition. Now that my husband has revealed his true form and is being taken west, I will never again dare act recklessly. I beg you to bestow the fan upon me again, so that I may turn over a new leaf, cultivate myself, and nurture my life.” The local god said, “Great Sage, since this woman thoroughly knows the method for extinguishing the fire, have her eradicate its root and then return the fan to her. Thus this humble god may dwell here in peace, save the people of this region, and receive some sacrificial offerings. That would truly be a gracious favor.” Pilgrim said, “When I asked the villagers before, they told me that fanning out the fire on this mountain brings only one year’s harvest before the flames break out again. How can it be eradicated at the root?” The Rakshasi replied, “To eradicate the root of the fire, you need only fan forty-nine times in succession, and it will never break out again.”

It was only because I behaved without openness or honor that so many forces had to be mobilized and put to such trouble.
We too have cultivated ourselves into human form; it is only that we have not yet attained the true fruition.
Now that my husband has revealed his true form and is being taken west, I will never again dare act recklessly.
I beg you to bestow the fan upon me again, so that I may turn over a new leaf, cultivate myself, and nurture my life.”

The local god said, “Great Sage, since this woman thoroughly knows the method for extinguishing the fire, have her eradicate its root and then return the fan to her. Thus this humble god may dwell here in peace, save the people of this region, and receive some sacrificial offerings. That would truly be a gracious favor.”
Pilgrim said, “When I asked the villagers before, they told me that fanning out the fire on this mountain brings only one year’s harvest before the flames break out again.
How can it be eradicated at the root?”

ja: よんじゅうきゅうかい
u.src: The Rakshasi replied, “To eradicate the root of the fire, you need only fan forty-nine times in succession, and it will never break out again.”

p.src: Hearing this, Pilgrim grasped the fan, exerted all his strength, and waved it forty-nine times in succession toward the mountaintop. Torrential rain poured down upon the mountain. It was indeed a treasure: rain fell wherever there was fire, while the sky remained clear wherever there was none. The master and his disciples stood where there was no fire and were not wetted by the rain.
